Majjanaśataka
stotra. Eulogizing Lord Raṅganātha a. Śrīraṅgam whose image is conceived a. being bathed with water. MD. 9001. 10184 (inc.). [Page-32b]

Majjanaśanivāravrata

Majjāgaṇapatikavaca
from Uttarakhaṇḍa of Gaṇeśapurāṇa. America 1049.

Majjhimanikāya
or Madhyamanikāya. Bud. Pāli. The 2nd book of the Suttapiṭaka, consisting of three books (each having pannāsa i. e., (pañcāśat suttas)); 150 discourses of Buddha. For its similarity with the Madhyama Āgama (Chinese), see Intro. xviii-xxiv of Nalanda edn. of the text.
Andhra Uni. 2663 (inc.). Colombo p. 48 (2 mss.). Colombo D. I. 69. 1760. Fausboll 44-48 (sns.). IO. Pāli p. 72 (no. 26). Kandy II. p. 1. Nanjio 542. Paris Pāli p. 32 (3 mss.; 1 inc.).
Pt.. (1). Ed. Freidrich Max Muller, The Sacred Books of the East. Oxford 1879. Vol. II. Pt. 2. (2). Ed. V. Trenckner, Academies. London Pali Text Society London, Copenhagen. 1888. (3). Ed. in 3 Vol.. in Siamese script. Bangkok, 1894. (4). Colombo, 1895-1914; 1908. (5). Upāli the Householder, a transl. from the Majjhimanikāya. by Bhikku Śilācāra. Buddhist Review I. 1909. iii. (6).
